brief: Two-storey, five-bay brick house with a low side-gabled roof and a small classical entrance portico on octagonal wooden columns; the real house (about 45 ft wide) is scaled to the lot keeping its symmetry. Stands behind an iron fence on one of Harrow Falls' older river streets near the courthouse. Record gap: 2 exterior/interior photos only.

facade.notes: the Frevart-Schnaitter House (1849): a symmetrical brick house, five bays, a portico of two columns over the door, a bracketed and dentilled cornice, shutters, ivy over the walls; a cast-iron fence with a gate and a straight walk to the door, a lamp post, flower beds

why.note: the Greek Revival's columned entry portico on a merchant's brick house
